subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app move toward a chat-first default or explicit chat-first mode, accept only focused Android UX/media/connectivity slices while keeping Overview-first, or leave chat-first Android clients as external forks for now?
rationale: Current main partially improves Android chat and media, but the remaining choice changes official mobile navigation, pairing expectations, media permissions, release/security posture, and contributor scope.

options.title: Scope focused Android slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define small launch/navigation, media, and connectivity PR slices with real-device proof before accepting implementation.

options.title: Keep Overview-first
options.body: Document that the official app remains an Overview/Gateway companion first and ask contributors to file only concrete defects or owner-approved enhancements.

options.title: Sponsor chat-first mode
options.body: A maintainer explicitly sponsors a chat-first default or mode and requires onboarding, upgrade, media-permission, and real-device validation before merge.

recommendation.title: Scope focused Android slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define small launch/navigation, media, and connectivity PR slices with real-device proof before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is primarily the official Android app product surface, and obviyus is the documented Android app maintainer with relevant feature history.
